entities.label: JUDGE

sentences.text: ORAL JUDGMENT Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied by the judgment and award dated 01st August, 2009 passed in Motor Accident Claims Petition No.1535 of 2000 passed by learned Presiding Officer & Fast Track Court No.2, Vadodara, the original claimants has preferred this First Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Petition No.1535 of 2000
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/969/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined 1.1
The original claim of the claimants was for Rs.05,00,000/-.
As against that, learned Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.03,66,000/- as under.

Sr. Particulars Amount (in Rs.)
 No.
 1 Future Loss of Income 03,36,000/-
 2000 X 12 X14 multiplier  2 Loss of consortium 25,000/-
 3 Funeral expenses 05,000/-
It is the case of the claimants that on 26 th July, 1999 the deceased was driving Tempo bearing Registration No.GJ-5-T-2223 on Dhulia road on the correct side.
However, the luxury bus bearing Registration No.GJ-7T-4464 was being driven rashly and negligently by its driver and dashed with the Tempo while coming on the wrong side.
The deceased received serious injuries and thereafter succumbed to those injuries.
The claimants being heirs and legal representatives of the deceased

,
approached the learned Tribunal for compensation for untimely death of the deceased by invoking the provision of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
3. The learned Tribunal, after having considered the pleadings and evidence on record, held the driver of the luxury bus as sole negligent for the accident in question.
The Tribunal thereafter proceeded to award compensation by considering the income of the deceased at Rs.03,000/- per month.
Keeping the age of the deceased at 25 years, the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/969/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined learned Tribunal has adopted multiplier of 14.
The learned Tribunal has further deducted one-third amount towards the personal expenditure.

Thus,
the learned Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.03,36,000/- under the head of future dependency (Rs.03,000/- X 1/3 X 12 X 14).

The learned Tribunal has thereafter awarded sum of Rs.25,000/-
under the head of consortium and Rs.05,000/- under the head of funeral expenses.

Thereby, in all,
Rs.03,66,000/- came to be awarded by the learned Tribunal towards the compensation.

4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid, the original claimants have approached this Court seeking, inter alia, enhancement in the compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have heard learned advocate Mr.N.R. Desai for learned advocate Mr.P.P. Majmudar for the appellants- claimants and learned advocate Mr.Rathin Raval for the respondent - insurance company.
6. Learned advocate for the appellants submitted that the award passed by the learned Tribunal granting compensation is on very lower side and thereby cannot be said to be adequate in nature.
Mr.Desai further submitted that the learned Tribunal has committed serious error in computing the income by not considering the future rise of income.

Learned advocate further submitted that considering the age of the deceased at 25 years, as per the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company limited v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680], 40% future rise ought to be considered.

entities.text: National Insurance Company limited v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned advocate NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/969/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined further submitted that admittedly the age of the deceased was 25 years and thereby relying upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [(2006) 9 SCC 121], multiplier of 18 ought to have been adopted by the learned Tribunal.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [(2006) 9 SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned advocate further submitted that deduction of one-third towards personal expenditure is also on higher side.
He submitted that considering number of dependents, it ought to be one-forth.

Learned advocate further relied on the judgments of the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), The New India Assurance Company Limited v. Smt.Somwati [(2020) 9 SCC 644], Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited v. Smt.Somwati [(2020) 9 SCC 644]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
[(2018) 18 SCC 130]
and Sarla Verma (supra) to submit that each dependent is entitled to Rs.40,000/- for loss of consortium.
6.1 By making above submissions, learned advocate Mr.Desai for the appellants has prayed this Court to allow the Appeal by enhancing the compensation adequately.

7. Per contra, learned advocate Mr.Rathin Raval for the insurance company vehemently opposed the present appeal contending that the judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal is just and proper and thereby may not be interfered with.

While raising all the material defence and submissions, learned advocate for the insurance company could not disputed the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), Smt.Somwati (supra), Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra) and Sarla Verma (supra).
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/969/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined 7.1
By making above submissions, learned advocate for the insurance company prayed this Court to pass appropriate order in accordance with law.
8. I have heard learned advocates for the respective parties and have gone through the record and proceedings of the learned Tribunal.
No other and/or further submissions have been canvassed by learned advocates appearing for the respective parties except what are stated hereinabove.

9. Having heard learned advocates for the respective parties and having gone through the material on record, a short question that falls for consideration of this Court is whether the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal could be said to be just and proper?

entities.text: Patil Ashaben Santoshbhai vs Vijaykumar Swaminath Sing
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So as to decide the aforesaid question, it would be apt to take into consideration the law laid down by the Apex Court in cases of Pranay Sethi (supra), Smt.Somwati (supra), Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra) and Sarla Verma (supra).
Keeping in mind the ratio of Apex Court laid down in the aforesaid cases, in my considered opinion, compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal cannot be said to be just and adequate.

I say so because while computing the income,
future rise of income requires to be considered.
The age of the deceased at the relevant time was 25 years and thereby 40% rise requires to be considered.

Considering the number of dependents,
deduction of one- fourth would be adequate under the head of personal expenditure.

Multiplier,
according to me, has to be 18 keeping NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/969/2012 JUDGMENT DATED:
20/01/2023 undefined in mind the age at 25 years of the deceased and all the dependents shall be entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the head of loss of consortium, Rs.15,000/- under the head of funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
I answer the question accordingly.

11. In view of the aforesaid discussion, judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal is,
therefore, required to be modified as under.

Particulars Amount (in Rs.)
Future Loss of Income 06,80,400/-
 [Rs.3000/ + Rs.1200/- (40%
 future prospectus) - Rs.1050/-
 (1/4 personal expenditure) X 12  X 18 (multiplier)
Funeral expenses 15,000/-
Loss of estate 15,000/-
Consortium 01,60,000/-
 Total 08,70,400/-
Amount already awarded 03,66,000/-
Additional amount to be paid 05,04,400/-
12.
Resultantly, the appeal is partly allowed.
The appellants - claimants shall be entitled to amount of Rs.05,04,400/- by way of additional compensation, to be paid with 6% interest, from the date of application till its realisation.

The insurance company is directed to deposit Rs.05,04,400/- with proportionate costs and interest before the learned Tribunal within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/969/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined 12.1
The appellants-claimants shall pay additional court fees accordingly.
13. The Tribunal shall issue Account Payee cheque in the name of the claimants after identification and proper verification.
Record & Proceedings, if any, to be sent back.
